title: Standard operators: SelectMany, grouping, joining
hook: Reporting an exam is flattening answers per attempt, grouping by question, and joining to a skill map — SelectMany, GroupBy, Join. Not three nested for-loops you cannot test.

sections.heading: Projection, flattening, grouping
sections.prose: Where filters. Select projects one-to-one. SelectMany projects one-to-many and concatenates; two from clauses are that operator. GroupBy is deferred and non-streaming: it consumes the source, then yields IGrouping<TKey,TElement>. OrderBy is the same buffering class. Redis cache invalidation lists keyed by tenant are a GroupBy. Attempt.Answers is a SelectMany. Prefer method syntax when the lambda needs an index overload that query syntax cannot say.

snippets.label: SelectMany then GroupBy on attempts
snippets.explanation: Select would yield sequences of answers. SelectMany yields answers. GroupBy buffers all answers before the first tuple appears.

sections.heading: Join and GroupJoin
sections.prose: Join is an inner equijoin: join skill in skills on answer.QuestionId equals skill.QuestionId. GroupJoin (join … into) keeps the outer element and an inner sequence that may be empty — a grouped left join you then flatten with DefaultIfEmpty for a true left outer join. Providers may ignore an orderby on a source before a join; sort after you have the result shape. Cache-aside lookups (id -> Redis payload) are usually a dictionary, not Join, when the inner sequence is already in memory and keyed.

snippets.label: Join answers to a skill catalog
snippets.explanation: equals is required; you cannot write == in the join clause. This is an inner join: answers with no skill row disappear.

interviewTakeaways: SelectMany flattens; Select of a collection does not.
GroupBy and OrderBy buffer; Where and Select stream.
Join is inner; GroupJoin plus DefaultIfEmpty is left outer.
join requires equals, not an arbitrary predicate.
commonPitfalls: Using Select when you meant SelectMany, then wondering why the type is IEnumerable<List<T>>.
Calling GroupBy then mutating the source before you enumerate the groups.
N+1 dictionary lookups inside a Select that should have been a Join or a ToDictionary first.

jsTsCorrelations.note: array.flatMap is SelectMany. Object.groupBy is eager. JS has no join operator in the language; you build maps. LINQ Join is typed and deferred.
